title: Kong Yingda
subtitle: 574–648 · early Tang classical scholar
shortSummary: Kong Yingda connects classical interpretation, collaborative compilation and state education, showing Confucian learning as both intellectual tradition and institutional project.
curatorialDescription: The classical project associated with Kong Yingda brought interpretation into a state undertaking. It did not merely preserve older texts; it made choices among commentarial traditions, standardised readings and educational uses.
The museum models figure, text, commentary and institution separately. This allows visitors to ask who compiled, which versions were used and where the work entered education.
His case also shows why Confucian traditions cannot be reduced to private ethics. Ritual order, schools, officials and textual interpretation all shaped historical influence.
researchNote: The compilation, revision and official circulation of the Correct Meaning involved multiple participants and stages. The first release uses approximate dates and does not present the project as a single-author book.
